title: Given the rate of AI game development, next-gen consoles could be expired out of the box. Instead of setting a console to download a 100GB+ game overnight, people will be prompting their console to create what game they want to play in the morning.
author: YzKatzFacts

comments.author: MAG1LIVE
comments.body: damn this is a new low

comments.author: FuckTheNitro
comments.body: If it can be like the giants game from enders game, maybe

comments.author: baroldnoize
comments.body: One caveat is people don't know what they want to play

comments.author: sirpalee
comments.body: Who will pay for the tokens to generate a game?

replies.author: YzKatzFacts
replies.body: Same way people pay for gamepass and ps plus membership, people would pay especially if a game console for first time is giving consumers the games they've been asking for.

replies.author: sirpalee
replies.body: Do you have any idea how much tokes does it take to make a game? Even simple indie games? Not one shotted prototypes, but something coherent and enjoyable.

replies.author: YzKatzFacts
replies.body:
Agreed, today a console like this probably would fail for that very reason, but who really knows how much of today's token usage and costs is being inflated for profit or is inefficient?

In time and with more competition, costs should stabilize.

Right now, the AI race is expensive, with these companies racing at full speed toward a finish line that nobody can identify.

replies.author: sirpalee
replies.body: There are definitely tons of things you can do to improve it. Right now its not feasible, in a few years maybe.

comments.author: BlueAndYellowTowels
comments.body:
I wouldn't get this. The whole point of buying games or playing other people's games is that you're going to be exposed to something new. You might try a new genre. You might be exposed to a new story.... there'a million unexpected things that can happen when you expose yourselves to new forms of art.

That will never happen with a technology you prompt for games. You're basically just making a content mill for yourself. No new idea. No unexpected ideas. Nothing. Just...game ideas from your brain.

To me, that sounds ridiculously boring.

replies.author: YzKatzFacts
replies.body:
The games people generate with such a console could just be the starting point; that person could further customize the game with their own personally created assets, using what was generated merely as a framework, and games made would be able to be released and played by others.

The great irony of using AI to create art is its soulless feel; as big as AI becomes, it will inevitably bring people right back to wanting that human touch, however flawed it may be.

replies.author: BlueAndYellowTowels
replies.body:
I think people haven't played the tape...

If I can generate a game from AI. Then anyone can generate a game from AI.

...and let's say I make a game and you play it. You like it except, you wish it had some other system in it to make it "more fun". You feed you LLM my game, it takes it remakes it and adds you system. Now, you're not playing my game anymore, you're playing whatever thing you've decided to turn my game into.

This the future we're talking about. A future where, any game can be anything without any effort and... like... that just completely diminishes the idea of what a video game is and why it's an engaging experience.

replies.author: YzKatzFacts
replies.body:
For better or worse, the gate of admission has been lifted; the future wave you are describing is very well known because it has been seen elsewhere. Today, so many have the tools to make a movie or become famous through YouTube or TikTok; Hollywood is no longer necessary.

Now, it is just the game industry's turn. Yet, you will see that there is nothing like the original, however advanced the remixes become. Authenticity cannot be outpriced or price-matched. Games by indie or AAA developers will still have their official standard version.

replies.author: BlueAndYellowTowels
replies.body: I agree with you overall point. But I don't agree with the idea that it's "authentic". I think most people who deeply care about art will consider AI created art inauthentic.
